question: Does any of the four numeric constructed lanes build its negatives by corrupting a DERIVED result over correct operands, rather than by substituting or misbinding an operand?
method: Two independent routes required to agree: (1) read the negative-construction code in each lane's builder; (2) load the built parquet and diff each negative claim against its paired positive over at least 100 sampled negatives per lane plus a full-lane operand-survival pass.

code_evidence.negative_construction: emit() renders the SAME template twice with only the numeral slot changed: label 1 takes spec['correct_value'], label 0 takes spec['cited_value'] (R17-H146_lane.py:246-262). build_row_misbind sets cited_value to the same column's cell in a DIFFERENT row; build_col_misbind sets it to a DIFFERENT column's cell of the same row. The asserted operand itself is replaced.
code_evidence.verbatim_docstring_claim: 'No derived values, no arithmetic, no traces. Every asserted numeral is present in the evidence' (R17-H146_lane.py:20-22)
code_evidence.audit_in_builder: verify()'s misbind_rederivation_audit re-derives each sampled negative's binding and requires cited_value != correct_value and a different (row, column) binding - i.e. it enforces operand substitution (R17-H146_lane.py:373-408)

data_evidence.reading: operand survival 0.0 across all 15,000 pairs - the numeral in the negative claim never equals the numeral in its positive twin. The single asserted operand is the thing that changed.

quant_misbind.derivation_finding: Every claim is a single-value assertion of the form 'The {col} of {key} is {v}.' - one numeral, no second operand, no stated result. The lane is structurally incapable of teaching derivation checking.

example_pair.evidence_excerpt: Match. Valladolid has a Match of 2, a Result of 2–0. Llagostera has a Match of 10, a Result of 6–1. Leganés has a Match of 13, a Result of 3–0. Osasuna has a Match of 15, a Result of 1–2. Lugo has a Match of 16, a Result of 1–1. Tenerife has a Match of 19, a Result of 1–2.

code_evidence.negative_construction: The emit loop builds pos_claim with p['unit'] and neg_claim with neg_unit over the identical value p['val'] (R18-H150_scaleunit_lane.py:1070-1071, 1086-1089). The swap is legal only inside a physical dimension (DIM), so the corrupted token is a unit of the same kind.
code_evidence.verbatim_docstring_claim: 'the byte-identical claim with ONE token replaced - a different unit of the SAME dimension. Digits never move' (R18-H150_scaleunit_lane.py:12-14)
code_evidence.note: The task's operand_substitution class names 'unit, scale' explicitly. The claim asserts one value carrying a unit; nothing is computed.

data_evidence.reading: operand survival 1.0 - the numeral is byte-identical across every pair; the token-level diff is always the unit phrase alone (e.g. 'kilometres' -> 'millimetres'). The perturbed element is the unit attached to the operand, not a computed result.

quant_scale_unit.derivation_finding: Every claim is a single-value-plus-unit assertion, 'The {col} of {key} is {val} {unit}.' - one numeral, no second operand, no stated result. Structurally incapable of teaching derivation checking.

num_compare.classification_caveat: The corrupted result is a RELATION (ordering / direction), never an arithmetic quantity. The class definition's first clause fits exactly - every operand stays correct and consistent with the evidence and only the asserted RESULT of an operation over them is corrupted - but the definition's parenthetical enumerates 'difference, sum, product, ratio, percentage', none of which this lane states. Under an arithmetic-only reading this lane is 'neither'. Both readings are given so the adjudicator can pick; the counts against the bar are reported for each.

code_evidence.negative_construction: emit() renders the identical template twice with only the relation word substituted: label 1 takes `word`, label 0 takes FLIP[word] (R20-H177_lane_B.py:325-336). Both operands are formatted into both legs from the same spec (va, vb), so no numeral moves.
code_evidence.verbatim_docstring_claim: 'the negative is decidable by reading and ordering two present values - there is no arithmetic anywhere in the lane' (R20-H177_lane_B.py:29-31); and 'Ordering is the one derivation subtype requiring zero computation' (line 16)
code_evidence.project_taxonomy_note: The lane's own registration classes ordering as a DERIVATION subtype: 'Gate 1 put 31.2% of finqa's derivation-class rank-loss mass on errors decidable by ORDERING two values the evidence already prints' (R20-H177_lane_B.py:14-16).
code_evidence.attestation_gate: assemble() rejects any candidate where the true relation word and its flip are not EQUALLY readable in the evidence (R20-H177_lane_B.py:419-422), which removes the option of settling the pair by matching the claim's word against the evidence.

data_evidence.reading: operand survival 1.0 over all 15,000 pairs - both numerals are byte-identical across the twin and both are present in the evidence (presence rate 1.0). The only token that moves is the relation word. In 14,750 of 15,000 negatives (98.3%) the relation is NOT stated anywhere in the evidence, so the label cannot be recovered by any attribution or string-matching check - it can only be settled by ordering the two operands. The 250 cmp_trend negatives are the exception: their direction is stated in the passage verbatim (rate 1.0), so those are also decidable by attribution.

num_compare.derivation_finding: The claim states a result computed from two other stated numbers - an ordering ('X (11) is greater than Y (5)') or a superlative over the serialised rows. It never states an arithmetic result: no difference, sum, product, ratio or percentage appears in any template (R20-H177_lane_B.py:126-154). So the lane teaches checking a COMPARISON over operands, and teaches nothing about checking an arithmetic computation.

code_evidence.negative_construction: Each family builder returns a pos/neg claim pair off one template with one element rebound (R20-H177_lane_C.py:156-234): role_swap reattaches the amount to a different labelled quantity; period_swap rebinds it to a different year the passage names; sign_swap flips the direction word of a change the passage states in words. The amount itself is never altered.
code_evidence.verbatim_docstring_claim: 'Gate 2 traced 54.9% of finqa's false-positive rank-loss mass to mislabeled operand role, sign or period rather than to wrong computation ... None of those needs arithmetic to detect - each is a BINDING failure over values the passage already prints' (R20-H177_lane_C.py:11-16)
code_evidence.sign_swap_is_attribution: change_statements() only admits a change whose direction the passage states in WORDS beside its magnitude - 'flipping the word is decidable from the evidence with no computation' (R20-H177_lane_common.py:312-318). One amount is carried, never two endpoints, so no ordering or arithmetic is available or needed.

data_evidence.reading: The sampled diff is a role phrase in role_swap ('income tax expense' -> 'recognized income tax benefit'), a year in period_swap ('2020' -> '2019'), a direction word in sign_swap ('decreased' -> 'increased'). The full-lane numeral-survival rate of 0.796 is entirely the period_swap family, whose corrupted token is a YEAR LABEL that the numeral extractor counts as a number - the monetary amount itself survives in every one of the 11,174 pairs. All 3,896 sign_swap negatives flip a direction the evidence states verbatim (rate 1.0), so that family is settled by contradicting stated text, not by computing anything.

num_rolebind.derivation_finding: Every claim carries exactly one monetary amount and no second operand - the rate of claims with three or more numerals is 0.0 across the lane. No template states a result over other stated numbers (R20-H177_lane_C.py:103-119). Structurally incapable of teaching derivation checking, including the ordering subtype.

bar.definition: count of lanes classified derivation_corruption or mixed; 0 of 4 -> supply gap recorded as the training-side cause; >= 1 of 4 -> signal exists

reading_dependency.note: The count turns on one judgement call, stated here rather than buried: whether a corrupted ORDERING counts as a corrupted derivation result.

arithmetic_results_only.basis: No lane's claim ever states a difference, sum, product, ratio or percentage computed from other stated numbers. Checked against every claim template in all four builders and against the built data.

material_qualification.evidence: No *_arm_run.py mix spec references R20-H177_lane_B.parquet or R20-H177_lane_C.parquet. Every arm from R18-H150 through R20-H175b loads exactly two numeric constructed lanes: R17-H146_lane.parquet as quant_misbind (30,000 rows) and R18-H150_scaleunit_lane.parquet as quant_scale_unit (5,540 rows).
material_qualification.consequence: On the mix as actually TRAINED, the count against the bar is 0 of 2 present lanes under either reading - the only lane carrying any derivation-shaped signal, num_compare, has never been in a training mix. The supply gap holds for every trained checkpoint regardless of how the ordering question is adjudicated.

code_data_disagreements: none - both routes agree on all four lanes
lanes_not_found: none - all four builders and all four parquet artifacts located on disk
anomalies: The task's premise says the training mix contains four numeric constructed lanes. It contains two. num_compare and num_rolebind are R20-H177 lane artifacts built 2026-08-16 and are not referenced by any arm-run mix spec.

A fifth numeric-adjacent lane, qrel_contrast (R20-H175b_qlane.parquet, 17,972 rows), IS in the R20-H175b mix, but its negatives flip the QUESTION rather than anything numeric, so it carries no derivation signal either. Reported for completeness; not classified, since the task named exactly four lanes.

In num_rolebind the full-lane numeral-survival rate reads 0.796 rather than 1.0. This is a measurement artifact of counting a YEAR as a numeral: period_swap's corrupted token is a four-digit year label. The monetary operand survives in 100% of pairs across all three families.
